analyzed_vuln.description: The OP_ADDI/OP_SUBI peephole constant-folding path rewinds to an earlier integer load and replaces it with `gen_int()` without preserving or validating intervening jump targets. The replacement may be longer than the original instruction. In this PoC, a 2-byte `OP_LOADI_3` is replaced by a 3-byte `OP_LOADI R1,15`, while an already-patched `or` jump still targets byte offset 5. That offset is now the replacement instruction's immediate byte (`0x0f`), so the VM interprets it as `OP_LOADI32`. Its operand decoding reaches the end of the 11-byte irep, and `NEXT` at vm.c:1183 reads `iseq[11]` one byte out of bounds. `scope_finish` only exposes the malformed control flow by shrinking the allocation to the exact bytecode length; it is not the root cause.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The fuzzer passes attacker-controlled Ruby source directly to `mrb_load_string`. Triggering requires control flow that creates and patches a jump target immediately after a compact integer-load instruction, followed by an `+=` or `-=` expression that enters `gen_move`'s constant-folding optimization and changes that load to a larger encoding. For `3or l=3\nl+=12\n1`, folding 3+12 changes the 2-byte specialized load into a 3-byte generic load but leaves the earlier `or` jump targeting its new immediate byte. Executing that branch decodes malformed bytecode and runs past the irep buffer.

args: Analyze the OP_ADDI/OP_SUBI constant-folding branch in gen_move() at mruby/mrbgems/mruby-compiler/core/codegen.c:624-643. What is the safest minimal condition using codegen_scope::lastlabel to prevent rewinding across an already established jump target, including the PoC `3or l=3\nl+=12\n1`? Is checking that the original integer instruction data0.addr is not before lastlabel sufficient, and are there other folding paths with the same rewind-across-label issue?

The reported crash occurs because gen_move identifies a sequence integer load, MOVE, ADDI/SUBI and rewinds s->pc to the integer load before calling gen_int. A previously patched `or` jump targets the byte immediately following the original compact OP_LOADI_3. Replacing the two-byte load with a three-byte OP_LOADI shifts/overwrites that target without updating the jump. Existing code only checks whether the ADDI instruction itself starts at s->lastlabel. I have inspected dispatch(), which sets s->lastlabel = s->pc when patching a jump, no_peephole(), gen_addsub(), gen_muldiv(), and gen_binop(). I suspect gen_move must reject folding whenever the sequence start is earlier than the most recent label (probably `addr_pc(s, data0.addr) < s->lastlabel` after decoding the original integer operand), then restore/generate the ADDI normally. Please assess label semantics and analogous code.
